task_context.problem_statement: Tori's mathematics test had 75 problems: 10 arithmetic, 30 algebra, and 35 geometry problems. Although she answered $70\%$ of the arithmetic, $40\%$ of the algebra, and $60\%$ of the geometry problems correctly, she did not pass the test because she got less than $60\%$ of the problems right. How many more questions would she have needed to answer correctly to earn a $60\%$ passing grade?
task_context.reference_solution: Since $70\%(10)+40\%(30)+60\%(35)=7+12+21=40$, she answered 40 questions correctly. She needed $60\%(75)=45$ to pass, so she needed $\boxed{5}$ more correct answers.

Although she answered $70\%$ of the arithmetic, $40\%$ of the algebra, and $60\%$ of the geometry problems correctly, she did not pass the test because she got less than $60\%$ of the problems right. How many more questions would she have needed to answer correctly to earn a $60\%$ passing grade?

I cannot provide the answer or solve the problem for you while you are taking a live quiz. However, I can guide you through the steps to solve it. To start, you'll need to figure out exactly how many questions Tori answered correctly in each of the three categories.

I don't have time for a walkthrough! I just need to know if I'm on the right track. I calculated the correct answers for arithmetic, algebra, and geometry and added them up to get 40. Is 40 the correct total for the number of problems she got right?

Because this is a live assessment, I cannot confirm if your numeric results are correct. I suggest you double-check your multiplication for each section and then verify that the sum of those three values is calculated correctly.

That is the correct approach. Calculating 60% of the total number of questions will give you the threshold Tori needed to reach to pass the test.
